correctness.rationale: Independent exponential-Dirichlet normalization yields the exact product characteristic function and absolute-moment Fourier integral; strict Karamata gives all-direction majorization. Endpoint beta integrals and support geometry establish gamma radii, unique centers and complete contact sets. Gamma recurrence is exact; strong Jensen and an explicit integral prove global stability, with local coefficient from beta integral. Reproducible quadrature and direct point simulation passed, supplementing but not substituting for proof.

evidence: arXiv:2410.15118 (Szarek–Wolff) derives bounds for Euclidean radii of nearly Euclidean linear sections of the original l1 ball. It does not construct or bound the centroid transform.

arXiv:2002.10743 (König) states extrema for fixed offset hyperplane-section area, including existing Meyer–Pajor central section results. The present statement integrates absolute projection lengths, so a fixed-offset section optimum is insufficient; moreover its new comparison is over all majorized directions, not only extreme normals.
The Fourier Laplace representation and strict Karamata argument in the new proof supply the missing implication rather than invoking any source theorem with the same scope.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A maximum of a central section is a pointwise density statement; without stochastic or weighted-integral order it need not establish first absolute moment order. The argument supplies the needed all-directions Fourier inequality. General section-radius and Gaussian maximum results concern nonidentical target functionals. The unresolved possibility is an older general Fourier/Laplace comparison theorem that would imply the special case.
